newsitem.title: USA: Hilton says ITT rejection "no surprise".
newsitem.headline: Hilton says ITT rejection "no surprise".

text.p: A Hilton Hotels Corp spokesman said Thursday that ITT Corp's rejection of Hilton's revised $70 per share bid came as no surprise to the company.
"There was never any attempt to have the shareholders have one word of say in this." said Marc Grossman, Hilton's senior vice president of corporate affairs.

Earlier, ITT's board unanimously recommended shareholders reject Hilton's offer, valued at $8.3 billion in cash and stock. The move was widely expected after Hilton boosted the original $55 per share, or $6.5 billion, offer made in January.

In a statement, ITT said it believes a merger could cannibalize operations of hotels and casinos located in the same markets as Hilton's. ITT also cited uncertainty about the value of Hilton's shares when exchanged for ITT shares, plus opinions of financial advisors as reasons for its rejection.

Hilton asserts that ITT shareholders should have a right to vote on its offer before ITT implements a plan to break up into three companies, buy back 26 percent of its shares for $70 a share and restructure its debt. The plan does not require a shareholder vote and if completed, could thwart Hilton's takeover effort.
